name: Copper Area Thermal
blurb: temperature rise of a power part from the copper area under it
intro: Treats the copper around the part as a round fin: heat spreads out through the copper and leaves both board faces by convection and radiation. It answers the junction temperature for a given area, and the area needed to stay under the limit. The bare FR4 around the pour is ignored, so the answer errs on the warm side.

inputs.label: Copper area (one layer)
inputs.help: 645 mm² = 1 in². A 25 × 25 mm pour is 625 mm².

inputs.label: Package thermal pad
inputs.help: Where the heat enters: DPAK tab ≈ 40, D2PAK ≈ 90, SOT-223 tab ≈ 11, 3×3 QFN pad ≈ 3.

inputs.label: Junction to board (θJB / θJC bottom)
inputs.help: From the datasheet: θJC(bot) for tab or exposed-pad parts.

examples.title: DPAK regulator dropping 1.5 W on 1 in² of 1 oz copper
3×3 QFN buck, 0.6 W, 4-layer board with stitched planes

usage: Give the dissipated power in W, ambient in °C, the copper area in mm² (per layer), the package thermal pad area in mm², copper weight in oz (0.5/1/2/3), the number of via-stitched layers carrying that area (1, 2 or 4), the package's junction-to-board resistance in °C/W, the maximum junction temperature and the air speed in m/s. It returns the copper-to-ambient thermal resistance, board and junction temperatures, the margin, the power allowed at this area and the area needed for this power, plus a sweep over area. Use it to size a copper pour under a DPAK, SOT-223 or exposed-pad part before reaching for a heat sink.
sources: Annular fin efficiency, Schmidt approximation η = tanh(m·r0·φ)/(m·r0·φ), φ = (R/r0 − 1)(1 + 0.35·ln(R/r0)); m = √(h/(k·t)) - Incropera & DeWitt, Fundamentals of Heat and Mass Transfer, ch. 3 (extended surfaces)
Simplified air correlations h = 1.42·(ΔT/L)^0.25 (natural, laminar vertical plate) and h = 3.93·√(V/L) (forced, laminar) - Ellison, Thermal Computations for Electronic Equipment
Radiation h_r = ε·σ·(Ts² + Ta²)(Ts + Ta), ε = 0.9 for solder mask
Cross-check: ≈ 55 °C/W for 1 in² of 1 oz copper around a DPAK tab in still air, in line with manufacturers' θJA-vs-pad-area curves (roughly 45–60 °C/W)
